statement: In recursive Bayesian estimation (Bayes filtering), the belief distribution is the probability distribution over the current unobserved state $\mathbf{x}_k$ conditioned on all sensor measurements up to the current timestep $\mathbf{z}_{1:k}$, given by the recursive update equation: $$p(\mathbf{x}_k | \mathbf{z}_{1:k}) = \frac{p(\mathbf{z}_k | \mathbf{x}_k) p(\mathbf{x}_k | \mathbf{z}_{1:k-1})}{p(\mathbf{z}_k | \mathbf{z}_{1:k-1})} \propto p(\mathbf{z}_k | \mathbf{x}_k) p(\mathbf{x}_k | \mathbf{z}_{1:k-1})$$ where the predicted belief distribution is given by: $$p(\mathbf{x}_k | \mathbf{z}_{1:k-1}) = \int p(\mathbf{x}_k | \mathbf{x}_{k-1}) p(\mathbf{x}_{k-1} | \mathbf{z}_{1:k-1}) d\mathbf{x}_{k-1}$$

symbols.meaning: true unobserved state at timestep k
sequence of measurements from timestep 1 to k
updated posterior belief distribution over the state at timestep k given measurements up to timestep k
predicted belief distribution over the state at timestep k conditioned on measurements up to timestep k-1
measurement likelihood at timestep k given current state
state transition probability distribution from timestep k-1 to k

properties.property: The predicted belief distribution is obtained by integrating the transition probability against the prior belief distribution: $p(\mathbf{x}_k | \mathbf{z}_{1:k-1}) = \int p(\mathbf{x}_k | \mathbf{x}_{k-1}) p(\mathbf{x}_{k-1} | \mathbf{z}_{1:k-1}) d\mathbf{x}_{k-1}$.
properties.why: marginalising out the previous states under the Markov assumption

properties.property: The updated belief distribution is proportional to the product of the measurement likelihood and the predicted state distribution: $p(\mathbf{x}_k | \mathbf{z}_{1:k}) \propto p(\mathbf{z}_k | \mathbf{x}_k) p(\mathbf{x}_k | \mathbf{z}_{1:k-1})$.
properties.why: the denominator $p(\mathbf{z}_k | \mathbf{z}_{1:k-1})$ is constant relative to $\mathbf{x}_k$ and serves as a normalization factor

properties.property: The normalization denominator evaluates to $p(\mathbf{z}_k | \mathbf{z}_{1:k-1}) = \int p(\mathbf{z}_k | \mathbf{x}_k) p(\mathbf{x}_k | \mathbf{z}_{1:k-1}) d\mathbf{x}_k$.
properties.why: the integral of the posterior probability density over all possible states must be unity

properties.property: If state transitions are linear and variables are normally distributed, recursive Bayesian estimation of the belief distribution reduces to the Kalman filter.
properties.why: linear Gaussian models preserve multivariate normal distributions across prediction and innovation steps

properties.property: The joint distribution over all states and measurements decomposes as $p(\mathbf{x}_0, \dots, \mathbf{x}_k, \mathbf{z}_1, \dots, \mathbf{z}_k) = p(\mathbf{x}_0) \prod_{i=1}^k p(\mathbf{z}_i | \mathbf{x}_i) p(\mathbf{x}_i | \mathbf{x}_{i-1})$.
properties.why: conditional independence of measurements and first-order Markov process dynamics

assumptions.assumption: The state sequence $\mathbf{x}_k$ is an unobserved first-order Markov process such that $p(\mathbf{x}_k | \mathbf{x}_{k-1}, \dots, \mathbf{x}_0) = p(\mathbf{x}_k | \mathbf{x}_{k-1})$.
assumptions.breaks_when: The state dynamics depend directly on older historical states $\mathbf{x}_{k-2}, \dots, \mathbf{x}_0$ beyond the immediate predecessor.

assumptions.assumption: The measurement $\mathbf{z}_k$ is conditionally independent of all past states given the current state: $p(\mathbf{z}_k | \mathbf{x}_k, \mathbf{x}_{k-1}, \dots, \mathbf{x}_0) = p(\mathbf{z}_k | \mathbf{x}_k)$.
assumptions.breaks_when: Measurements depend on historical states or sensor noise is temporally correlated across timesteps.

failure_modes.signature: Posterior distributions acquire increasingly complex functional forms over time that cannot be integrated or maintained recursively in closed form
failure_modes.cause: Measurement likelihood functions whose product with the predicted distribution does not belong to a tractable or conjugate parametric family

failure_modes.mode: Continuous loss of certainty (dispersion of belief)
failure_modes.signature: Continuously decreasing certainty / increasing spread in the belief distribution about position or state
failure_modes.cause: Propagating motion over time without receiving informative sensor measurements to innovate the belief distribution
